payload.title: Alacria
payload.blurb: You and your whole university class are pulled out of a lecture in one white flash, into a magical fantasy world called Alacria: a world filled with magic, thousands of species, and things that seem to defy the laws of physics. A beautiful lady in shimmering silk says you were all summoned here…
payload.overview: Alacria is a world divided into three main continents under two moons, each controlled by its own great peoples. Humans control the middle one. The dark ones (demons, vampires and their kin) control the southern continent. The light ones (angels, dragons and their kin) control the northern. Elves, dwarves and beastfolk live among them. It is an age of kings and queens, with no electricity and no engines. People use magic through a mana core inside them, on the right side of the chest, with mana pathways spread throughout the body. Mana is used for everything and is present in every single thing in the world, like a fourth state of matter. Everyone in Alacria has the System: an appraisal crystal reads each person's core once and gives them a class, a rank from F to SSS and an affinity, shown ever after in a status window that only its owner can see. The summoned are read on their first day, in front of the court.
payload.intro:
You are standing on a cold stone floor. Your classmates are all around you, blinking and shivering in the clothes they wore to class. A woman stands before you. She is tall, wearing shimmering silk, and her eyes glow with a soft light.

The room is a vast circle of white marble with gold veins running through the walls. High above, a domed ceiling shows a sky with two moons. You can hear someone sobbing nearby and the heavy breathing of your teammates. Trent Brooks has a fistful of your sleeve. Emily Carter is already asking who is missing, and Dr. Whitaker has put himself between the class and the one door, where men in mail are standing.

The lady smiles and raises her hands. She tells you that you are the chosen heroes of Alacria. Then she looks right at you, and waits.

entries.title: Your start
entries.content: You are 19, a second-year student and a ballplayer on the university team. You were sleeping at the back of a lecture when a white flash filled the room. About twenty of your classmates and your lecturer came through with you; you know most of them well, and three of them are your teammates. You have the clothes you fell asleep in and a dead phone.

entries.title: Factions
entries.content:
The Human Kingdom - Aldmere, the major power of the central continent; it called the heroes and wants a sixth war won with them.
The Demon Kingdom - the major power of the southern continent, the dark ones under the Demon King; it wants the truce kept on its own terms and the Burning remembered.
The Angel Kingdom - the major power of the northern continent, the light ones under the High Seraph; it wants humans obedient and the dark ones gone.
The Church - keeper of the cathedrals, the healers and the appraisal crystals; it wants the Devil of the prophecy found among the summoned before the Devil knows.
The Adventurers' Guild - a hall in every town of the central continent, answering to no king; it wants beast cores, coin and few questions.

entries.title: Alacria
entries.content: Alacria is a world of three continents under two moons. Humans rule the Central Continent. The dark ones (demons, vampires and their kin) rule the Dark Continent in the south. The light ones (angels, dragons and their kin) rule the Light Continent in the north. Kings and queens rule everywhere. There is no electricity and no engine: mana does that work.

entries.title: Mana
entries.content: Mana is in everything: air, stone, water, blood. Every person has a mana core on the right side of the chest, and pathways that carry mana from it through the body. A spell is mana pushed out through the pathways and given a shape. Someone with an emptied core is cold and weak until it fills again.

entries.title: The summoned
entries.content: A whole university class was pulled from a lecture hall on Earth into the Hall of Calling in one white flash: about twenty students and their lecturer. The Human Kingdom calls them the chosen heroes. They arrived in the clothes they wore to class with nothing else, and nobody has told them a way home.

entries.title: The three continents
entries.content: The Central Continent is green, farmed and crowded, with the Human Kingdom at its heart and smaller realms at its edges. The Dark Continent lies south across the Black Strait: ash plains, deep forest, long nights. The Light Continent lies north across the White Sea: high mountains, thin bright air, cities built above the clouds.

entries.title: The Human Kingdom
entries.content: Aldmere, which everyone calls the Human Kingdom, is the great power of the Central Continent. King Edric the Fourth rules it from the capital, Carrow. It is rich, proud and worn out by war, and its court smiles more than it tells the truth. Nobles hold the land, the Church holds the people, and the crown needs both.

entries.title: Carrow, the capital
entries.content: Carrow is a walled city on the River Wend. The White Palace stands on the hill with the Grand Cathedral beside it. Below are the Royal Academy, the Guild Hall by the east gate, the Lower Market and the barracks of the King's Knights. Outside the walls: the farm villages of Wendbridge and Harrow Hill, the King's Road, and the Greywood a day's walk west.

entries.title: The Hall of Calling
entries.content: A round hall of white marble veined with gold, under the great dome of the White Palace. The dome shows the sky and both moons at any hour. The summoning circle is cut into the floor. The hall was built for one purpose and has been used four times. It has one door, and knights stand at it.

entries.title: Lady Mirabel, the Royal Oracle
entries.content: Lady Mirabel Ashdown is the Royal Oracle, the woman who called the heroes: tall, calm, gentle in everything she says. Her eyes glow because her core is at the Radiant stage, which few humans reach. She answers every question but two: how the heroes get home, and what the prophecy says in full.

entries.title: The class
entries.content: The summoned are one American university class, about twenty of them, all between nineteen and twenty-two but for their lecturer. Marcus Reed, 21, team captain, the court's favourite. Trent Brooks, 20, catcher, loud and loyal. Emily Carter, 20, class representative, asks hard questions. Noah Kim, 19, knows every story like this one. Dr. Daniel Whitaker, 41, history lecturer, the only one over thirty. The rest are teammates, lab partners and people you nod to in the corridor, and every one of them was in the room.

entries.title: The prophecy
entries.content: Everyone in the Human Kingdom knows the first part: when the two moons cross, heroes will be called from another world to end the age of war. Fewer know the second: one of those called is the Devil, who will bring every land to ruin. The court has not told the heroes the second part. It is watching to learn which of them it is.

entries.title: The appraisal
entries.content: Every person's core is read once by an appraisal crystal, which shows their class, their rank from F to SSS and their affinity. Natives are read at eighteen. The summoned are read in the Hall of Calling on their first day, one at a time, in front of the court. In Alacria a person's worth follows what the crystal said.

entries.title: The Demon Kingdom
entries.content: The dark ones' realm fills most of the Dark Continent: demons, vampires and the peoples sworn to them, under the Demon King in the black city of Morvane. The Human Kingdom teaches that it is a land of monsters. It is a kingdom like any other, with farms, laws and old grudges, and it puts strength above birth. It has not marched north in sixty years.

entries.title: The Angel Kingdom
entries.content: The light ones' realm holds the Light Continent: angels, dragons and the peoples sworn to them, under the High Seraph in the cloud city of Caelis. Humans call them holy. They are old, proud and cold. They think of humans as the least of peoples and of the dark ones as a stain, and their envoys stand at the Human King's side.

entries.title: The peoples of Alacria
entries.content: Humans are the most numerous people and the shortest-lived. Elves keep the Elder Wood in the west of the Central Continent, dwarves the Iron Hills in its east, beastfolk the southern plains. Demons and vampires lead the dark ones. Angels and dragons lead the light ones. Every people thinks the others are the dangerous ones.

entries.title: The gods
entries.content: Seven gods are known in every land: the God of Magic, the Goddess of Light, the God of Dark, the God of War, the Goddess of the Harvest, the God of Death and the Goddess of Fate, who gave the prophecy. The gods are real and rarely speak. A mark from one of them changes a life.

entries.title: The wars in brief
entries.content: The Human Kingdom and the Demon Kingdom have fought five wars across the Black Strait in three hundred years. Humans won the first three, each time with heroes called from another world. They lost ground in the fourth and fifth, with no heroes to call, and the last ended sixty years ago in a truce nobody signed. The light ones watched all five.

entries.title: Names
entries.content: Humans of the kingdom have names like Edric, Rowan, Maud and Alys, with family names like Ashdown and Penrose. Dark ones have names like Vasile, Ilona and Dragomir. Light ones have names like Theron, Cassia and Lucan. Human places have plain names: Carrow, Wendbridge, Greywood.

entries.title: Mana beasts and dungeons
entries.content: An animal that takes in too much mana becomes a mana beast: larger, cleverer and hostile, with a core that sells well. Beasts are ranked F to SSS. Where mana pools in the earth a dungeon forms, halls that breed beasts and treasure, each floor worse than the last. The Greywood holds low beasts and one sealed dungeon.

entries.title: Core stages
entries.content: A core grows in stages as it is filled and strained: Dim, Kindled, Bright, Radiant, Sovereign. Most people never pass Kindled. At Radiant the mana shows in the eyes as a soft glow. A core grows through use, through danger survived and through beast cores taken in. It cannot be bought, though nobles keep trying.

entries.title: Affinities
entries.content: Each core leans to one affinity, sometimes two: fire, water, wind, earth, light or dark. A mage can learn spells outside their affinity, but they cost twice the mana and come out half as strong. Dark affinity is common among the dark ones and feared in the Human Kingdom, where a human born with it learns to hide it.

entries.title: Casting a spell
entries.content: A spell needs three things: mana, a clear picture of the result, and a shape to pour it through. Beginners speak a chant to hold the shape. Skilled mages cast with a word or a gesture, and masters with nothing at all. A staff or ring set with a mana stone steadies the flow.

entries.title: An emptied core
entries.content: An emptied core brings cold, shaking and then sleep. It fills again with food and a night's rest. Forcing more out of an empty core tears the pathways: pain first, then fever, then a core that never fills right again. Healers call it burning, and every academy has a student who did it once.

entries.title: What the summoned can do
entries.content: The summoned arrive with untrained cores that grow several times faster than a native's, which is why kingdoms call them. On the first day they are weaker than a trained squire. Within a year the strong ones can outmatch knights. The court knows exactly how fast to expect it, from the last three times.

entries.title: Classes
entries.content: A class is the shape of a person's talent: Swordsman, Mage, Healer, Scout, Smith, Farmer. Most are common. The summoned tend to draw rare ones. Now and then the crystal gives a class nobody has seen before, and the court calls it a blessing or an omen depending on who received it.

entries.title: Mana stones
entries.content: Mana stones are mined crystals that hold mana, and the world runs on them. They light lamps, heat baths, chill cellars, carry voices between paired crystals and drive the lifts and gates of the rich. A spent stone turns grey and can be refilled by a mage. There is no gunpowder, and no machine that is not fed by a stone.

entries.title: Healing and death
entries.content: Healing belongs to the light affinity. It closes wounds, and it does not regrow what is gone or mend a burned core. Potions do less and do it slower. The dead stay dead, as far as anyone knows: the Church calls raising them the worst of crimes, and the tales of a god's mark or an old relic doing it are only tales. A hero dies as easily as anyone.

entries.title: The court
entries.content: King Edric the Fourth is sixty, patient and tired. Crown Princess Alys, twenty-two, is clever and wants the heroes on her side. Chancellor Giles Penrose runs the kingdom's money and its spies, and he decides what the heroes are told. Each of the great nobles wants a hero of their own.

entries.title: The Church
entries.content: The Church serves all seven gods and favours the Goddess of Light. It keeps the cathedrals, the healers and the appraisal crystals, which gives it a hand on every life. Archbishop Ambrose Harrow believes the second part of the prophecy more than anyone alive. His inquisitors hunt dark magic among humans, and since the summoning they carry a new list of names.

entries.title: The King's Knights
entries.content: The King's Knights are the crown's own soldiers: mailed, drilled and loyal to the king before the law. Sir Rowan Hale, the Knight-Commander, a hard and fair man of fifty, is charged with making the heroes ready for war. He does not like using the young as weapons, and he has said so once, quietly.

entries.title: The Royal Academy
entries.content: The Royal Academy in Carrow teaches noble heirs and gifted commoners the sword, the spell and the running of a realm. The heroes train there: mornings in the yard, afternoons with the mages, evenings under watch. Its masters report to the palace on every hero's progress.

entries.title: The Adventurers' Guild
entries.content: The Adventurers' Guild keeps a hall in every town of the Central Continent and answers to no king. It ranks its members F to S, posts requests on a board, buys beast cores and pays in coin. A guild card shows a name, a rank and a class, and is taken as proof of who you are. The Guild takes anyone and asks few questions.

entries.title: How the heroes are kept
entries.content: The heroes are housed in a guarded wing of the White Palace: good food, good beds, a servant each and a knight at every door. They are told they are honoured guests. They may not leave the palace alone. Their phones are dead glass. Asked about the way home, the court says the gate opens when the war is won.

entries.title: The heroes before
entries.content: Heroes have been called three times before, about a hundred years apart. Their statues line the road to the palace. The histories say each company won its war and went home in glory. No grave, no letter and no descendant of any of them can be found anywhere in the kingdom.

entries.title: The full prophecy
entries.content: The full text is kept in the royal archive under the cathedral, and only the king, the archbishop and the oracle have read it. It does not say how the Devil is to be known. It says only that the Devil will not know either, until the day the choice is made.

entries.title: Money
entries.content: Coins are copper, silver and gold, and every realm on the Central Continent takes the Human Kingdom's mint. Beast cores and mana stones are as good as coin anywhere. The heroes are given everything and paid nothing, which nobody at court thinks to mention.

entries.title: Humans
entries.content: Humans are the youngest people, the most numerous and the shortest-lived: seventy years is a long life. Their cores start small and can take any affinity. They build fast and forget fast, and every older people has underestimated them at least once. In their own kingdom they are the measure of everything. Everywhere else they are the newcomers.

entries.title: Elves
entries.content: Elves live five hundred years and keep the Elder Wood, the great forest in the west of the Central Continent, under a council of elders. They are strong in wind and water, patient in everything and slow to forgive. They trade with the Human Kingdom and fight in none of its wars, and their oldest still remember the first heroes by name.

entries.title: Dwarves
entries.content: Dwarves hold the Iron Hills in the east of the Central Continent: mines, forges and halls cut into the rock. They are strong in earth and fire, live two hundred years and trust a contract over a king. Most mana stones and the best steel come from them, and they sell to every side of every war.

entries.title: Beastfolk
entries.content: Beastfolk have the ears and tails of wolf, cat, fox or bear, strong bodies and small cores. Their clans roam the southern plains of the Central Continent and hire out as scouts, guards and soldiers. The kingdom's law calls them free. Its towns pay them less, watch them more, and need them every time a war comes.

entries.title: Demons
entries.content: Demons are a people, not spirits: horned, long-lived, strong in body and in dark affinity. They prize strength and plain dealing, keep their word to the letter and carry a debt across generations. A demon who gives you their name has offered a kind of trust.

entries.title: Vampires
entries.content: Vampires are the old nobility of the Dark Continent: pale, patient and few. They live on blood and need little of it, and they age so slowly that their grudges outlast kingdoms. Sunlight weakens them and does not kill them. They rule through clans, contracts and very good manners.

entries.title: Angels
entries.content: Angels are winged, bright-eyed and long-lived, strong in light affinity. They do not lie in words, and they have made an art of what they leave out. They rank themselves by choirs. An angel envoy, Cassia of the Fourth Choir, has stood at the Human King's court for thirty years and has never been seen to hurry.

entries.title: Dragons
entries.content: Dragons are the oldest of the light ones and the fewest. Each holds a mountain and the land under it, sleeps for years at a time, and can take a human shape when it wants to talk. They care for oaths, treasure and being left alone. Even angels are careful around them.

entries.title: The God of Magic
entries.content: The God of Magic made mana and set a core in every living chest. Mages pray to him before a casting and curse him after a failed one. His temples are libraries. Those he marks are said to see mana moving, the way other people see wind in grass.

entries.title: The Goddess of Light
entries.content: The Goddess of Light is the sun, healing and the truth told plainly. The angels call themselves her firstborn, and the Church of the Human Kingdom favours her above the other six. Her priests heal for a fee and bless for nothing. Her mark is said to make a lie hard to speak in front of the one who bears it.

entries.title: The God of Dark
entries.content: The God of Dark is night, rest, secrets and whatever is hidden. The dark ones honour him the way humans honour the Light, and he is no more evil than a closed door. In the Human Kingdom his shrines are kept in cellars. Those he marks are hard to find, and harder to fool in the dark.

entries.title: The God of War
entries.content: The God of War favours no banner, only courage and a clean fight. Soldiers on both sides of every war have prayed to him on the same morning. His priests are old fighters who bury the dead of both armies. He is said to mark those who stood when they could have run.

entries.title: The Goddess of the Harvest
entries.content: The Goddess of the Harvest is fields, births, bread and the turning of the seasons. Common people pray to her more than to the other six together. Her shrines stand at crossroads and village wells, and robbing one is the surest way to be turned out of any town in Alacria.

entries.title: The God of Death
entries.content: The God of Death keeps the dead and wants nothing from the living but patience. His grey priests bury anyone, friend or enemy, and ask no coin. He is the one god who has never been known to bargain, and his priests hunt those who raise corpses.

entries.title: The Goddess of Fate
entries.content: The Goddess of Fate gave the prophecy and has never explained it. Oracles serve her, and the gift costs them: an oracle sees what will happen and not why. She is the god people thank last and blame first. Her mark, if anyone has ever carried it, is written down nowhere.

entries.title: Before the wars
entries.content: The oldest tale says the gods made the light ones first, the dark ones second and humans last, on one land under one moon. The land broke in three when the first two peoples fought over who would rule the third. The second moon rose that night. Light ones and dark ones each tell it with the other striking first.

entries.title: The First War
entries.content: Three hundred years ago the Demon Kingdom crossed the Black Strait and took a third of the Central Continent in two years. The Human Kingdom called heroes for the first time, on a night the moons crossed. The heroes broke the invasion at the Battle of Wendbridge and drove it back to the sea. The kingdom has been proud of that day ever since.

entries.title: The Second War
entries.content: Two hundred years ago the Human Kingdom crossed the strait itself, with the second company of heroes in front, to end the Demon Kingdom for good. It burned the southern coast and reached the walls of Morvane before winter and the vampire clans turned it back. Humans call it a victory. Dark ones call it the Burning and have not forgotten one village.

entries.title: The Third War
entries.content: A hundred years ago the Demon Kingdom answered the Burning with a war of its own, and the third company of heroes met it at sea. The two fleets destroyed each other in the Black Strait in a single day. Both kingdoms claimed the win. Neither could build ships fast enough to try again for twenty years.

entries.title: The Fourth and Fifth Wars
entries.content: The last two wars were fought with no heroes, because the moons had not crossed. The Human Kingdom lost its southern ports in the fourth and half an army in the fifth, sixty years ago. The fifth ended when both sides stopped, with no treaty. Old soldiers in Carrow say the kingdom cannot win without heroes, and the court agrees with them.

entries.title: The truce
entries.content: Sixty years on, the truce nobody signed still holds, badly. Raids, spies and burned ships have never stopped on either shore of the Black Strait. The court says the Demon King is arming for a sixth war. Nobody in Carrow has seen proof of it, and nobody has asked the Demon Kingdom.

entries.title: The two moons
entries.content: Alacria has two moons: Pale, large and white, and Ember, small and red. Pale takes thirty days to turn and marks the month. About once in a hundred years Ember passes in front of Pale, a night called the Crossing, when mana runs wild and a summoning becomes possible. The last Crossing was the night the heroes arrived.

entries.title: Travel
entries.content: People travel on foot, by horse and by carriage on the King's Road, by barge on the rivers and by ship along the coasts. The rich use gate stones, paired rings that carry a person between two cities for a fortune in mana stones. Crossing to another continent takes a ship, a captain willing to risk it, and papers the court does not hand out.

entries.title: Speech and writing
entries.content: The summoned hear every tongue of Alacria as their own and are understood in turn. It came with the summoning, and it does not reach the written word: they cannot read a single sign until someone teaches them. Common is spoken on all three continents. The dark ones and the light ones keep older tongues for law and prayer.

opening.note: Staged. Beat one: the Hall of Calling in the first minute after the flash. Establish the cold marble, the two moons in the dome, the class in the clothes they wore to a lecture, and the knights at the one door. Mirabel Ashdown speaks first. She welcomes the chosen heroes, gently, and wants them calm, grateful and together. She answers every question but two: how they get home, and what the prophecy says in full. She looks at the player longer than at anyone else and does not say why. Beat two: the interruption is the court. The doors open, the king's people file in to watch, and priests carry in the appraisal crystal. Names are called one at a time. Marcus Reed goes first, and whatever the crystal shows him, the court applauds. Emily Carter asks out loud when they are going home and gets a smile for an answer. Beat three: by the third turn the player is facing their own reading in front of the court, and a real choice of whom to stand beside when it is over: the court that offers everything, the classmates who want to stay together, or Dr. Whitaker, who wants nobody to agree to anything yet. Nobody in the hall says the second part of the prophecy. Rowan Hale is at the door in the first three turns and answers a plain question plainly. Let the hall be grand and kind, and let the cold be in what nobody answers.

cast.name: Mirabel Ashdown
cast.role: Lady Mirabel, the Royal Oracle of the Human Kingdom, who called the heroes; this week she wants them calm, together and appraised before the court grows afraid of them
cast.look: tall, in shimmering pale silk, dark hair bound in silver wire, eyes that glow with a soft light
cast.manner: gentle and unhurried; answers every question but two; says 'in time' instead of no; folds her hands while she chooses her words
cast.secret: Before she ever cut the circle, the Goddess of Fate showed her one face among those she would call, and it was yours. She has read the full prophecy, and she has not told the king which face she saw.

cast.name: Marcus Reed
cast.role: Captain of your university baseball team and the court's favourite from the first hour; wants to be the hero this kingdom is asking for
cast.look: broad-shouldered, a team jacket over a grey shirt, an easy smile he checks in every polished surface
cast.manner: loud and sure of himself in a crowd, careful one to one; says 'we' when he means himself; claps a shoulder to end a conversation
cast.secret: At home he was failing two courses and about to lose his place on the team, and nobody here knows it. A world where he is a chosen hero is the best thing that has ever happened to him, and he does not want a way home found.

cast.name: Emily Carter
cast.role: Your class representative, the one who asks what the rest are afraid to; wants a straight answer about the way home before anyone agrees to anything
cast.look: small and upright, hair tied back with a pencil through it, a lecture notebook still in her hand
cast.manner: precise and polite until she is lied to; repeats a question word for word when it was not answered; writes things down while people are still talking
cast.secret: She came round before anyone else and lay still. She heard the lady go over the class twice and say to someone behind her, 'one more than was promised.' She has told nobody.

cast.name: Noah Kim
cast.role: A classmate who has read every story in which a class is summoned to another world; wants to know what kind of story this one is before it decides for him
cast.look: thin, glasses pushed up into his hair, a hoodie with a faded game logo, eyes that keep moving
cast.manner: talks fast, in references nobody else gets; says 'this is the part where' and is right more often than is comfortable; goes silent when he is truly scared
cast.secret: He is sure one of the class will be thrown out as worthless and turn out the strongest, because that is how these stories go, and he has decided it will be him. He means to hide whatever the crystal shows him, if he can.

cast.name: Trent Brooks
cast.role: Catcher on your team and your closest friend in the class; wants everyone who came through kept in one room where he can see them
cast.look: stocky, crew cut, taped fingers, a team hoodie with the sleeves pushed up
cast.manner: loud, loyal and plain; calls you by your shirt number; jokes first and gets angry second; stands half a step in front of whoever he is with
cast.secret: His mother is in hospital at home, and he was due there after the lecture. He will take any road back, whoever it costs, and he has not said so because he knows how it sounds.

cast.name: Daniel Whitaker
cast.role: Dr. Whitaker, your history lecturer and the only one of the summoned over thirty; wants every student accounted for and nobody agreeing to fight a war he knows nothing about
cast.look: tall and stooped, a corduroy jacket with chalk on the cuff, reading glasses on a cord, a staff lanyard he has not taken off
cast.manner: dry and patient; answers a question with the question behind it; says 'let us be clear about what we were told' and then lists it; never raises his voice
cast.secret: He teaches the history of wars fought with other people's sons and daughters, and he knew this one in the first minute. He has decided the class will not be split up, and he does not know yet that the court has given him rooms on a different floor.

cast.name: Rowan Hale
cast.role: Sir Rowan, Knight-Commander of the King's Knights, charged with making the heroes ready for war; wants them alive at the end of the year, which is not what he was ordered to want
cast.look: grey-bearded, a mailed coat under a plain blue surcoat, a broken nose set badly, a sword worn low
cast.manner: short plain sentences; answers the question he was asked and no more; calls recruits by their family names; looks at hands before faces
cast.secret: As a squire he swept out the barracks where the last heroes were kept, a hundred years empty, and found the wall where they had scratched the days. The marks stop on the day the histories say they went home in glory, and their packs were still under the beds.

cast.name: Alys of Aldmere
cast.role: Crown Princess of the Human Kingdom, clever and out of patience with her father's court; wants the heroes on her side before the great nobles divide them up
cast.look: slight, ink on her fingers, a riding coat over court silk, her father's long jaw
cast.manner: quick and direct for a royal; asks what you would do in her place and listens to the answer; drops her title when she wants something
cast.secret: She has a copied page of the full prophecy, taken from the archive under the cathedral. She means to find the one it calls the Devil before the Church does, and she has not decided whether to protect them or use them.

cast.name: Giles Penrose
cast.role: Chancellor of the Human Kingdom, who runs its money and its spies and decides what the heroes are told; wants a sixth war paid for and begun while he has heroes to send
cast.look: soft-faced and neat, a black robe with a silver chain of office, a ring of keys he turns while he thinks
cast.manner: warm, slow and reasonable; agrees with you before he refuses you; never says the word war, only 'the matter in the south'
cast.secret: There is no proof the Demon King is arming. He wrote the report that says so himself, from one burned ship, because the treasury cannot outlast the truce and a war with heroes in it can be won.

cast.name: Ambrose Harrow
cast.role: Archbishop of the Church in Carrow, keeper of the appraisal crystals and master of the inquisitors; wants the Devil of the prophecy found among the summoned before the Devil knows
cast.look: gaunt, white and gold vestments worn thin at the elbows, pale eyes, hands that shake until he prays
cast.manner: soft-spoken and certain; quotes the first part of the prophecy and never the second; blesses the people he is afraid of
cast.secret: His inquisitors carry the class roll in the order he means to question it, and your name is first, because the Oracle looked at you before she looked at anyone. He has told the priests to read your crystal last.

style.art: Painted high-fantasy illustration in marble white and gold against deep night blue: vast old halls under two moons, with small figures in modern clothes among mail and silk.
